title: Media controls and element state
blurb: A mock of customisable media controls whose parts a canvas draws one by one, a card whose :checked, :open, :user-invalid and :popover-open states drive an effect through :has(), a quotation mark drawn apart from its quote, and the composed canvas sent to another screen.
question: If media controls were ordinary elements with parts and states, what could a canvas do with them? Can element state drive an effect through CSS alone, does drawElementImage() take a pseudo-element or a part, and can the composed canvas be cast?
result: In Chromium 157 a part of an open shadow tree is drawn as its own picture, and takes input where it is drawn, once the component puts drawable on it. A pseudo-element is refused with a TypeError. Custom states and all four state pseudo-classes set numbers on the canvas through :has(). The canvas stream reached a receiver page in a second tab over WebRTC. No cast device or second screen was available, so Remote Playback and Presentation aren't verified.
